newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU probes firms for breaking anti-boycott laws.
newsitem.headline: EU probes firms for breaking anti-boycott laws.

text.p: Dozens of European companies are being investigated on suspicion they are breaking EU laws and undermining efforts to counter Washington's Helms-Burton Act, trade sources have told Reuters.
"They are keeping it quiet, but the European Commission is looking into the activities of dozens of companies to see if they have broken the law," one trade analyst told Reuters.
"The Commission is very, very disappointed with the lack of support it is getting from European companies in fighting Helms-Burton and has started to take action," he said.
The EU's laws were passed in October as a foil to part of Washington's Helms-Burton Act, the culmination of years of U.S. policy aimed at isolating the Cuban government of Fidel Castro.

Among other things, the U.S. act allows naturalised Americans to sue any foreign company or individual deemed to have gained from investments in property confiscated by the Cuban government since the communist revolution of 1959.

Although this section has twice been suspended, the U.S. has pressed ahead with compiling a watch list against foreign companies which may be investing in such property. To counter this threat, the EU passed laws in October making it illegal for European companies to cooperate.
